Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk We are exposed to the following financial risks connected with our operations: • credit risk related to our financing activities; • currency risk; and • interest rate risk. We seek to monitor and manage these risks through established policies, procedures, and risk‑mitigation practices. The quantitative data reported in the following sections does not have any predictive value. In particular, the sensitivity analysis on market risks does not reflect the complexity of the market or the reaction, which may result from any changes that are assumed to take place. Credit Risk Our credit concentration risk differs in relation to the activities carried out by the segments and end markets in which we operate; the risk is partially mitigated by the large number of counterparties and customers. Considered from a global point of view, however, there is a concentration of credit risk in trade receivables and receivables from financing activities, in particular dealer financing in the European Union market and in North America, as well as in South America for Agriculture and Construction. Financial assets are recognized in the statement of financial position net of write-downs for the risk that counterparties may be unable to fulfill their contractual obligations, determined using available information on customer creditworthiness and historical data. The maximum credit risk to which we were theoretically exposed at December 31, 2025 is represented by the carrying amounts stated for financial assets in the statement of financial position and the nominal value of the guarantees provided on debt or commitments of third parties. 37 Dealers and final customers are generally subject to specific assessments of their creditworthiness under a detailed scoring system. In addition to carrying out this evaluation process, we may also obtain financial and non-financial guarantees for risks arising from credit granted for the sale of equipment and related parts. These guarantees are further secured, where possible, by retention of title clauses or specific guarantees on financed equipment sales to the distribution network and on equipment under finance or leasing agreements. Balances that are determined to be uncollectible, in whole or in part, are written down on an individual basis when they are significant. The amount of the write-down is based on an estimate of the recoverable cash flows and the date of receipt, the costs of recovery, and the fair value of any guarantees received. Impairment losses are recognized for receivables that are not written down on a specific basis, but rather determined based on historical experience and statistical information. passages.heading: Debt note
passages.text: Credit Facilities Lenders of committed credit facilities have the obligation to make advances up to the facility amount. Lenders of uncommitted facilities have the right to terminate the agreement with prior notice to CNH. At December 31, 2025, CNH's available committed unsecured facilities expiring after twelve months amounted to $ 6.5 billion, of which $ 1.3 billion for Financial Services ($ 5.5 billion at December 31, 2024, of which $ 1.2 billion for Financial Services). Euro 3.25 billion Revolving Credit Facility: On April 19, 2024, the Company terminated its five-year committed revolving credit agreement dated March 18, 2019 (as amended and restated on December 10, 2021) and entered into a new five-year credit agreement, which provides for an unsecured, committed revolving credit facility in an aggregate principal amount equal to € 3.25 billion. The Company may elect to increase the total commitments under the credit facility up to an additional € 500 million on the terms set forth in the credit agreement. In March 2025, the Company extended the maturity date by one year on the terms set forth in the credit agreement. As such, the credit agreement will mature and all 93 outstanding loans will become due and payable on April 19, 2030, or such later date as may be extended pursuant to a remaining one-year extension option which is available to the Company on the terms set forth in the credit agreement. The credit facility contains customary covenants (including a negative pledge, a status (or pari passu ) covenant and restrictions on the incurrence of indebtedness by certain subsidiaries) and customary events of default, some of which are subject to minimum thresholds and customary mitigants (including cross acceleration provisions, failure to pay amounts due or to comply with certain provisions under the credit agreement, the occurrence of certain bankruptcy-related events) and mandatory prepayment obligations upon a change in control of the Company. At December 31, 2025, the Company was in compliance with all covenants in the credit agreement. At December 31, 2025, Financial Services' committed asset-backed facilities expiring after twelve months amounted to $ 3.7 billion ($ 3.7 billion at December 31, 2024), of which $ 3.5 billion at December 31, 2025 ($ 3.1 billion at December 31, 2024) were utilized. Repurchase Agreement We are a party to a Global Master Repurchase Agreement which expires in September 2026. As of December 31, 2025, the Company had sold, and not yet repurchased, CAD 450.0 million ($ 328.7 million) of Canadian receivables under the repurchase agreement, with an obligation to repurchase such receivables in 30 days. The repurchase agreement is treated as a financing arrangement for accounting purposes. credit_strengths.text: CNH's operating cash flow has strengthened materially over the annual trend, rising from a lower base to a level that comfortably covers reported cash interest costs. This improving cash generation supports the company's ability to service its financing obligations and fund working capital needs across its agricultural and construction equipment segments.

The company maintains substantial committed unsecured credit facilities expiring beyond twelve months, including a large European revolving facility and asset-backed commitments for its financial services arm. This deep liquidity access provides flexibility to refinance maturities and supports the captive financing business that underpins equipment sales.

key_risks.text: CNH carries significant credit concentration in dealer and customer financing receivables, particularly in Europe and North America, with a substantial portion of financing receivables subject to write-downs. A deterioration in dealer creditworthiness or used equipment values could trigger elevated impairment charges and strain the financial services segment's profitability.

The debt structure includes a large revolving credit facility maturing in the medium term, a repurchase agreement with a near-term repurchase obligation, and commercial paper programs. Refinancing risk is manageable given committed facilities, but reliance on short-term funding for the captive finance book exposes the company to rollover and interest rate risk.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage, measured as operating income over cash interest paid, sits well below the sector median, indicating that earnings currently provide a thinner cushion relative to peers. The declining operating income trend over recent years has compressed coverage, and a further earnings downturn could pressure the company's ability to meet fixed charges from operating profits alone.

Operating cash flow exceeds reported cash interest paid by a comfortable margin, suggesting that core operations generate sufficient liquidity to cover interest obligations. However, the absence of a complete debt figure and capital expenditure data limits a full assessment of free cash flow after mandatory investments and shareholder distributions.

overall_credit_view.text: CNH's credit profile reflects a large-scale industrial franchise with captive financing operations, but operating income has declined across the annual trend, and interest coverage is materially weaker than the sector median. The company's leverage position cannot be fully assessed because debt is not tagged in the available data, which is a material gap for evaluating refinancing risk and capital structure.

Liquidity is supported by substantial committed facilities and a sizable cash balance, while shareholder distributions absorb a portion of internally generated funds. Our forward-looking view is that credit quality will depend on stabilizing industrial demand, managing captive finance credit losses, and maintaining access to committed bank lines to refinance maturing obligations.

credit_strengths.text: CNH 的營運現金流按年度趨勢已顯著增強，由較低基數上升至能輕鬆覆蓋所報告現金利息成本的水平。此現金產生能力的改善，支持公司履行其融資責任的能力，並為其農業及建築設備分部的營運資金需求提供資金。
公司維持大量承諾無抵押信貸融資，到期日超過十二個月，包括一項大型歐洲循環融資及其金融服務部門的資產支持承諾。此深厚的流動性渠道提供靈活性以再融資到期債務，並支持支撐設備銷售的專屬融資業務。

key_risks.text: CNH 在經銷商及客戶融資應收賬款方面存在顯著信貸集中，尤其是在歐洲及北美，其中相當部分融資應收賬款須計提減值。經銷商信譽或二手設備價值的惡化可能引發減值費用上升，並對金融服務分部的盈利能力構成壓力。
債務結構包括一項中期到期的巨額循環信貸融資、一項附有近期回購責任的回購協議，以及商業票據計劃。鑑於已承諾融資，再融資風險屬可控，但專屬金融賬簿依賴短期資金，使公司面臨展期及利率風險。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率（以營運收入除以已付現金利息計算）遠低於行業中位數，顯示盈利目前相對同業提供的緩衝較薄。近年營運收入下降趨勢已壓縮覆蓋率，而盈利進一步下滑可能對公司僅憑營運利潤應付固定費用的能力構成壓力。
營運現金流超出所報告已付現金利息，幅度舒適，顯示核心業務產生足夠流動性以覆蓋利息責任。然而，缺乏完整債務數字及資本開支數據，限制了對強制投資及股東分派後自由現金流的全面評估。

overall_credit_view.text: CNH 的信貸狀況反映其具備大規模工業業務及專屬融資業務，但營運收入按年度趨勢下降，且利息覆蓋率明顯弱於行業中位數。公司的槓桿狀況無法全面評估，因為可用數據中債務並未標籤，這對評估再融資風險及資本結構而言是一項重大缺口。
流動性由大量已承諾融資及可觀現金結餘支持，而股東分派吸收部分內部產生資金。我們的前瞻性觀點是，信貸質素將取決於穩定工業需求、管理專屬融資信貸損失，以及維持取得已承諾銀行額度以再融資到期責任。
